tldr: MedAgent-Pro is an agentic reasoning framework that decouples medical diagnosis into disease-level guideline-based planning (via RAG) and patient-level step-by-step evidence-based reasoning with quantitative tool integration, outperforming mainstream VLMs and medical agentic systems.
contributions: Proposes MedAgent-Pro, the first agentic paradigm with systematic evidence-based reasoning for medical diagnosis aligned with modern clinical workflows.
Introduces a hierarchical structure with disease-level planning (RAG-based guideline retrieval) and patient-level reasoning (quantitative analysis and evidence-based verification).
Validates comprehensively across 10+ imaging modalities, 20+ anatomies, and 50+ diseases, showing superior performance over VLMs, agentic systems, and task-specific models.
methods: MedAgent-Pro employs a hierarchical workflow: at the disease level, a RAG agent queries a domain-specific knowledge base built from MedlinePlus (1,000+ disease entries, 4,000+ articles) to generate standardized diagnostic plans with clinical indicators and tool assignments. At the patient level, the system orchestrates step-by-step execution of the plan, invoking specialized tools (segmentation models like MedSAM, grounding models, and LLM-based coding tools) for quantitative analysis. An evidence-based reasoning paradigm evaluates the reliability of each step via a VLM-implemented state assessment function, assigning Continue/Terminate/Complete status before final diagnosis.
results: MedAgent-Pro outperforms GPT-4o by 34.0% in balanced accuracy and 55.3% in F1 score on glaucoma diagnosis (REFUGE2), and by 21.0% in bAcc and 44.2% in F1 on heart disease diagnosis (MITEA). On the NEJM dataset (10+ modalities, 50+ diseases), it achieves an overall improvement of 7.9%, with a 13.7% average gain on chest X-ray tasks. It also surpasses task-specific SOTA models by 6.8% AUC on glaucoma diagnosis despite zero-shot VLM use. Ablation studies show planning improves performance significantly, quantitative analysis increases F1 by 34.5% (glaucoma) and 20.7% (heart disease), and evidence-based reasoning provides further gains. Qualitative analysis with a domain-specific model (VisionUnite) showed only marginal improvement over GPT-4o.
limitations: Non-clinical images (e.g., everyday photographs) often lack compatible tool support, limiting performance in those cases.
The approach relies on visual tool availability, which is not universal across all imaging domains.
The knowledge base is built from MedlinePlus, which may not cover all medical conditions comprehensively.
VLMs in MedAgent-Pro remain zero-shot, potentially limiting specialized domain expertise compared to fine-tuned models.
